title: The #1 Rule of Good API Design

scenes.say: What’s the single rule that makes or breaks your API design in interviews?

scenes.label: Resource
scenes.sub: APIs organize data as resources—like users or orders.
scenes.say: First, APIs organize data as resources. Think users, orders, or products.
You act on resources using HTTP verbs. Get reads, post creates, put replaces, delete removes.
Here’s the trick: GET, PUT, and DELETE are idempotent. Repeat them, and nothing breaks. POST isn’t. That matters for reliability.

scenes.title: Standard Responses
scenes.say: Always use standard status codes. Two hundred for success, two oh one when you create something.

scenes.label: Version
scenes.sub: Use /v1/ or headers to avoid breaking old clients.
scenes.say: When you need to change things, version your API. Use slash v one, or headers, so old clients keep working.

scenes.question: Is POST idempotent?
scenes.wrong: Yes, it is safe to retry POST.
scenes.right: No. Only GET, PUT, and DELETE are idempotent. POST can create duplicates.
scenes.say: Here’s a classic interview trap: Is post idempotent? No—only get, put, and delete are. Post can create duplicates if retried.
